**C) Fused males remain fully independent of the female.**

After fusion, the male becomes little more than an attached sperm-producing appendage, entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream. "Fully independent" reverses that dependence into its opposite. Independence would require a free-living male with his own survival system; the text says he survives only through her blood. That one-way dependence is the decisive overturning fact, not a detail you can soft-pedal past.

**Trap:** Fusion language can sound like a partnership of equals; the passage ends on one-way dependence.

The claim fails because the male is "entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream for survival."

**D) Squid release glowing mucus purely to attract prey.**

Paragraph 4 says certain squid release clouds of glowing mucus or ink to startle and disorient predators, buying time to escape. Attraction of prey belongs to the anglerfish lure earlier; here the mucus is defensive, not a hunting bait, and "purely to attract prey" invents the wrong purpose. The startle-and-escape sequence is the stated job of the glowing cloud, so swapping in prey attraction misassigns the function. Mixing the anglerfish lure from paragraph 3 into paragraph 4's defence scene is the classic cross-section slip.

The claim fails: glowing mucus is deployed "to startle and disorient predators," not to lure prey.

**E) The 2020 survey recorded over 350 distinct species.**

Paragraph 6 reports that a 2020 ROV survey recorded bioluminescent responses across more than 350 distinct species. "Over 350" faithfully restates "more than 350" without inflating the count. The statement does not invent a larger total or claim every deep-sea animal was sampled—only that the survey crossed that species threshold. Keeping the year and the "more than 350" floor aligned makes this a clean quantity match.

The 2020 survey total in paragraph 6 matches the statement.
highlights: a light-emitting molecule called luciferin reacting with oxygen in the presence of an enzyme, luciferase
a much smaller male permanently fuses to the body of a female
entirely dependent on the female's bloodstream for survival
certain squid release clouds of glowing mucus or ink to startle and disorient predators
recorded bioluminescent responses across more than 350 distinct species

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Counter-illumination erases a fish's downward-facing shadow.
Glowing species proportions declined sharply with depth.
Ostracods display species-specific courtship flash patterns.
The luciferin-luciferase reaction has no laboratory applications.
The 2020 survey extended to roughly 4,000 metres.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Counter-illumination erases a fish's downward-facing shadow.**

Paragraph 5 defines counter-illumination as a faint underside glow matching dim downwelling light, effectively erasing the shadow a body would cast when viewed from below. That is precisely the downward-silhouette problem the technique solves. The glow is tuned to the light filtering from above so predators looking upward lose the dark outline. "Downward-facing shadow" is just another way of naming that underside silhouette against brighter water.

Paragraph 5's "erasing the shadow" wording matches the claim.

**B) Glowing species proportions declined sharply with depth.**

The 2020 survey found that the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of the depth range rather than declining steadily as researchers first expected. "Declined sharply" invents the trend the passage explicitly rejects. The expected decline is mentioned only as the outdated hypothesis the data failed to confirm. Consistency across depth is the result; "declined sharply" is the opposite story.

**Trap:** Expectation of decline is mentioned only as the outdated hypothesis, not as the result.

The claim fails because the proportion "remained remarkably consistent … rather than declining steadily."

**C) Ostracods display species-specific courtship flash patterns.**

Paragraph 7 notes that researchers studying ostracods have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays. The statement compresses that finding without adding a new claim about the unknown neurological mechanism. It stays with what was documented—the flash patterns in courtship—and does not pretend the timing circuitry is fully mapped. That restraint keeps the paraphrase faithful to the "documented … courtship displays" line.

The ostracod courtship line in paragraph 7 supports the statement.

**D) The luciferin-luciferase reaction has no laboratory applications.**

Paragraph 8 says the reaction has been adapted into a widely used laboratory tool for gene-expression markers and calls the technique genuinely indispensable in molecular biology and medical research. "No laboratory applications" flatly denies that lab career. A tool that tags proteins so cells glow under lab conditions is by definition a laboratory application. Absolute "no" wording cannot survive next to "widely used" and "indispensable."

The claim fails: the passage calls the tool "genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research."

**E) The 2020 survey extended to roughly 4,000 metres.**

Paragraph 6 places the encounters between the surface and roughly 4,000 metres depth. The statement simply restates that depth ceiling. It does not invent a deeper limit or claim the survey ignored shallow water; the range still runs from the surface down to that figure. Restating "roughly 4,000 metres" keeps the depth bound inside the survey sentence.

The survey's depth range in paragraph 6 matches the claim.
highlights: effectively erasing the shadow their bodies would otherwise cast when viewed from below
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of that entire depth range rather than declining steadily
complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays
a technique that has become genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research
between the surface and roughly 4,000 metres depth

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether an inference is actually supported, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Independent evolution implies bioluminescence offers strong survival value.
If 76% of deep species glow, most remain fully dark.
The "burglar alarm" effect implies marked predators become targets.
Counter-illumination implies matching light helps avoid detection.
Fused anglerfish males imply females gain no reproductive benefit.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Independent evolution implies bioluminescence offers strong survival value.**

Paragraph 1 stresses that deep-sea organisms reinvented glow on dozens of separate occasions, calling it one of the most repeatedly reinvented traits in the animal kingdom. Traits that keep evolving independently under aphotic conditions are the textbook footprint of strong adaptive payoff, not a one-off fluke. The inference does not invent a new experiment; it reads the repeated reinvention as evidence of usefulness. In a lightless habitat, that pattern points to survival advantage rather than accidental ornament.

**Tip:** "Repeatedly reinvented" is the cue that the inference is about advantage, not about one shared gene.

Independent reinvention across lineages supports reading bioluminescence as strongly useful for survival.

**B) If 76% of deep species glow, most remain fully dark.**

"As many as 76%" glowing already identifies a clear majority of bioluminescent animals. Inferring that most remain fully dark flips the arithmetic: the non-glowing remainder is the minority. Roughly one quarter without self-light cannot be "most," so the inference reverses the majority share the passage states. Once 76% is treated as the glowing majority, "most remain fully dark" cannot stand.

**Trap:** 76% can be misread as a minority if you fixate on the incomplete quarter instead of the percentage itself.

The inference fails because a 76% glowing share means most do not remain fully dark.

**C) The "burglar alarm" effect implies marked predators become targets.**

Paragraph 4 describes crustaceans ejecting particles that stick to an attacker and mark it as a conspicuous target for larger secondary predators—the "burglar alarm" effect. The nickname itself encodes the marked-predator → next-predator chain. The particles do not merely startle; they make the attacker visible to something bigger nearby. That secondary-target logic is exactly what the inference draws from the nickname and the "conspicuous target" wording.

The burglar-alarm description in paragraph 4 supports that marked predators become targets.

**D) Counter-illumination implies matching light helps avoid detection.**

By matching downwelling light and erasing the body's shadow against the brighter water above, counter-illumination stops predators from spotting silhouettes from below. Matching light is therefore a concealment tool, not a display. The predators searching upward for silhouettes are the detection threat the glow is designed to defeat. Avoiding that silhouette read is the same as helping the animal go unnoticed from below.

Paragraph 5's silhouette-erasing logic supports the avoidance inference.

**E) Fused anglerfish males imply females gain no reproductive benefit.**

The fusion turns the male into a permanently attached sperm-producing appendage on the female. That arrangement secures continuous access to sperm for the female; saying she gains "no reproductive benefit" contradicts the whole point of the strategy. The male's loss of independence is the cost he pays, not proof that she gains nothing. A living sperm source fused to her body is itself the reproductive payoff the passage describes.

**Trap:** "Appendage" and "dependent" describe the male's loss of independence, not a reproductive null for the female.

The inference fails because permanent attachment supplies ongoing fertilisation, a clear benefit to the female.
highlights: making it one of the most repeatedly reinvented traits in the animal kingdom
as many as 76% of animals living below this depth are capable of producing their own light
a conspicuous target for larger, secondary predators lurking nearby, a strategy researchers have nicknamed the "burglar alarm" effect
effectively erasing the shadow their bodies would otherwise cast when viewed from below by predators searching upward for silhouettes
the male becomes little more than a permanently attached sperm-producing appendage

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Independent evolution helps explain why chemical mechanisms vary between species.
The 350-species survey supports the point about consistent depth-wide glowing.
Defensive glowing and lure-based glowing serve identical evolutionary purposes.
Counter-illumination and lure-based hunting both directly cause visible light.
Laboratory use of luciferin shows deep-sea study benefits other fields.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Independent evolution helps explain why chemical mechanisms vary between species.**

Paragraph 1's dozens of independent origins sit next to paragraph 2's note that molecular details vary considerably between unrelated species. Separate evolutionary inventions naturally leave different luciferin–luciferase chemistries rather than one frozen pathway. If lineages reinvented the glow many times, there is no reason their molecular kits would be identical. That bridge from multiple origins to varying details is the synthesis the two paragraphs invite.

Linking independent origins to chemical variety is a fair cross-section synthesis of paragraphs 1 and 2.

**B) The 350-species survey supports the point about consistent depth-wide glowing.**

Paragraph 6's survey of more than 350 species is the evidence base for the finding that glowing-species proportions stayed remarkably consistent across depth. The headcount and the consistency claim are one result, not two unrelated facts. You cannot detach the "more than 350" tally from the depth-consistency conclusion that follows in the same survey sentence. Treating the species total as support for the consistency point is therefore a legitimate synthesis of that paragraph.

The 350-species survey in paragraph 6 directly backs the depth-consistent glowing claim.

**C) Defensive glowing and lure-based glowing serve identical evolutionary purposes.**

Anglerfish dangle a glowing lure to attract prey (paragraph 3), while paragraph 4 opens by saying bioluminescence serves purposes well beyond luring prey and then details defensive mucus and burglar-alarm marking. Attracting food and deterring or tagging predators are different jobs. "Identical" collapses those jobs into one, against the passage's "well beyond luring prey" pivot into defence. Shared light emission does not equal shared evolutionary purpose.

**Trap:** Both uses emit light, so it is easy to collapse them into one "purpose"; the passage separates lure from defence.

The synthesis fails: defence and prey-luring are explicitly different functions.

**D) Counter-illumination and lure-based hunting both directly cause visible light.**

The anglerfish lure is a glowing bait, and counter-illumination produces a faint underside glow. Whatever their ends, both mechanisms emit visible light the animal can control or sustain. One use draws prey; the other hides a silhouette—but both still put light into the water. The shared "cause visible light" claim is therefore a fair synthesis of paragraphs 3 and 5 without forcing their purposes to match.

Both strategies in paragraphs 3 and 5 produce visible light, so the shared-emission claim holds.

**E) Laboratory use of luciferin shows deep-sea study benefits other fields.**

Paragraph 8 moves from marine glow chemistry to a lab gene-expression marker that has become indispensable in molecular biology and medical research. That is the passage's own bridge from deep-sea chemistry to other sciences. Attaching a bioluminescent marker so cells glow under lab conditions is the concrete cross-field payoff. The synthesis does not invent a new application; it follows the paragraph's move from ocean chemistry into molecular biology and medicine.

Paragraph 8's laboratory adaptation shows deep-sea bioluminescence feeding other fields.
highlights: the precise molecular details vary considerably between unrelated species
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent across most of that entire depth range
Bioluminescence serves purposes well beyond luring prey. Many species use it defensively
females dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths to attract curious prey
The luciferinluciferase reaction has been adapted into a widely used laboratory tool

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had the survey not included deeper zones, fewer species would have been recorded."
"Researchers recommended that the team documents each flash pattern."
"The number of catalogued species continue to rise yearly."
"Neither the pressure nor the darkness were easily overcome."
"Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new hypothesis."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had the survey not included deeper zones, fewer species would have been recorded."**

This is inverted third conditional: Had + past participle stands in for If the survey had not …, and the result uses would have been recorded. The negative condition and past counterfactual result stay aligned. Fronting Had the survey not … is simply the inverted form of If the survey had not …, not a tense error. The would have been recorded result clause is the standard past-counterfactual payoff for that structure.

**Tip:** Had + past participle at the front is a standard exam signal for inverted third conditionals.

The inversion and would-have result are sound, so the sentence is grammatically fine.

**B) "Researchers recommended that the team documents each flash pattern."**

After recommended that, formal English wants the subjunctive base form: document, not documents. The -s turns the clause into ordinary present and breaks the mandative pattern. Recommend that + subject + base verb is the rule; documents looks correct only if you forget the mandative trigger. Spotting recommended that is the cue to strip the -s from the next verb.

**Trap:** documents looks like ordinary third-person agreement after the team, which is exactly why the error hides.

The sentence fails; repair to "… that the team document each flash pattern."

**C) "The number of catalogued species continue to rise yearly."**

The grammatical subject is the number, which is singular, so the verb must be continues. Continue matches the plural species distractor instead of the head noun. Of catalogued species is only a prepositional phrase modifying number; it never becomes the subject. Agreement tracks the head the number, so singular continues is required.

**Trap:** of catalogued species sits next to the verb and tempts plural agreement; ignore the of-phrase.

The sentence fails; repair to "The number of catalogued species continues to rise yearly."

**D) "Neither the pressure nor the darkness were easily overcome."**

With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Darkness is singular, so the line needs was, not were. The extract's corrected key treats this as false for that proximity rule. Pressure and darkness are both singular nouns; proximity still picks darkness, so were is wrong either way you count. Exam English follows the nearer noun after nor, not a "two things = plural" instinct.

**Trap:** Neither … nor often feels "plural" because two things are named; exams still follow the nearer noun.

The sentence fails; repair to "Neither the pressure nor the darkness was easily overcome."

**E) "Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new hypothesis."**

The participle Having observed correctly attaches to scientists, the people who did the observing and then proposed the hypothesis. There is no dangling modifier onto an inanimate subject. The observers and the proposers are the same plural noun, so the opener and the main clause share one logical subject. That clean attachment is what makes the participial sentence grammatical.

The participial opener matches its subject, so the sentence is grammatically fine.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the vehicle descended than lights began flashing."
"The technique, along with related methods, were adopted widely."
"Each of the recorded species have shown distinct flash timing."
"By the time results arrive, models will have already changed."
"The samples, which were gathered over months, reveal consistent patterns."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the vehicle descended than lights began flashing."**

No sooner … than is a fixed inversion pattern: had + subject + past participle in the first clause, than introducing the second event. The timeline (descent, then flashing) is clean. Using when or that instead of than would break the idiom; here than is correctly in place. The inverted had the vehicle descended is the expected companion to No sooner at the front.

The no-sooner inversion is correctly formed, so the sentence is fine.

**B) "The technique, along with related methods, were adopted widely."**

The head subject is the technique (singular). The along with related methods phrase is parenthetical and does not make the subject plural, so were should be was. Commas set the along with material aside; they do not create a compound subject the way and would. Agreement therefore stays with the technique, requiring singular was.

**Trap:** related methods after the comma looks like a plural subject, but along with never joins subjects the way and does.

The sentence fails; repair to "The technique, along with related methods, was adopted widely."

**C) "Each of the recorded species have shown distinct flash timing."**

Each of takes a singular verb: has shown, not have shown. Species is the object of of, not the agreement controller. Each forces singular even when the of-phrase names many items. Replacing have with has restores the rule without changing the meaning of the sentence.

**Trap:** species looks plural and sits beside the verb; each still forces singular.

The sentence fails; repair to "Each of the recorded species has shown distinct flash timing."

**D) "By the time results arrive, models will have already changed."**

By the time + present (arrive) pairs naturally with future perfect (will have already changed) for completion before a future reference point. The aspect fits a finished change ahead of the results' arrival. Present arrive marks the future landmark; will have already changed places the models' shift before that landmark. That by-the-time + future-perfect pairing is the standard tense frame for this meaning.

Future perfect after by the time is the right frame, so the sentence is fine.

**E) "The samples, which were gathered over months, reveal consistent patterns."**

Samples is plural, so were in the relative clause and reveal in the main clause agree. The non-restrictive which-clause does not disturb the plural head. Both verbs stay plural because they still answer to samples, not to months. Matching were and reveal to the same plural subject keeps the grammar consistent end to end.

Plural agreement holds throughout, so the sentence is fine.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "aphotic" means receiving abundant sunlight.
In Paragraph 3, "dangle" means to hang loosely, swinging.
In Paragraph 4, "conspicuous" means easily noticed or visible.
In Paragraph 5, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.
In Paragraph 8, "indispensable" means unnecessary and easily removed.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "aphotic" means receiving abundant sunlight.**

Paragraph 1 introduces the aphotic layer as the zone of near-total darkness after sunlight fades below roughly 200 metres. Aphotic labels the lightless realm, so "abundant sunlight" is the antonym of the context. The word sits in apposition to near-total darkness, which locks the sense to absence of light. Reading abundant sunlight into aphotic simply reverses the definition the paragraph supplies.

The claim fails: aphotic sits next to "near-total darkness," not abundant light.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "dangle" means to hang loosely, swinging.**

Female anglerfish dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths. In that hunting scene, dangle is the familiar "hang loosely / suspend" sense, not a figurative stretch. The lure hangs in front of the mouth as bait, which is ordinary physical dangling. No specialised marine jargon is needed; the everyday hanging meaning fits the sentence.

The lure sentence in paragraph 3 matches that hanging meaning.

**C) In Paragraph 4, "conspicuous" means easily noticed or visible.**

Particles stick to a predator and mark it as a conspicuous target for larger secondary predators. A target that must be easy for other hunters to spot is by definition easily noticed. The burglar-alarm strategy only works if the marked attacker stands out, which is what conspicuous encodes. Easily noticed or visible is therefore the context-true gloss, not a stretch.

Paragraph 4's "conspicuous target" use matches "easily noticed or visible."

**D) In Paragraph 5, "counterintuitively" means matching common expectations exactly.**

The sentence begins "Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage"—light as hiding aid runs against the everyday expectation that light reveals. Matching expectations exactly would need intuitively, not counter-. The counter- prefix is the clue that the claim goes against common sense, not with it. Camouflage-by-light is the surprise the adverb flags.

The claim fails: counterintuitively signals against expectation, not agreement with it.

**E) In Paragraph 8, "indispensable" means unnecessary and easily removed.**

The lab technique is called genuinely indispensable across molecular biology and medical research. Indispensable means essential; "unnecessary and easily removed" flips that into the opposite. Genuinely before indispensable intensifies how hard the tool is to do without, not how optional it is. The offered gloss is therefore the antonym of the paragraph's wording.

The claim fails: indispensable in paragraph 8 means the tool cannot be done without.
highlights: near-total darkness, a zone marine biologists call the aphotic layer
whose females dangle a glowing lure directly in front of their mouths
effectively marking that predator as a conspicuous target
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
a technique that has become genuinely indispensable across modern molecular biology and medical research

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "deploying" means releasing or putting into use.
In Paragraph 6, "remarkably" means unremarkably or without any surprise.
In Paragraph 7, "documented" means recorded through careful observation.
In Paragraph 3, "fuses" means separates completely and permanently.
In Paragraph 9, "comprehensively" means only partially or incompletely.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "deploying" means releasing or putting into use.**

Organisms trigger flashes, "deploying their light with a precision that suggests deliberate behavioural control." Deploying here is active use of the light tool, not merely possessing it. Precision and deliberate control only make sense if the animal is putting the glow into action on cue. Releasing or putting into use is therefore the context-true reading of that verb.

Paragraph 2's controlled-flash wording matches "releasing or putting into use."

**B) In Paragraph 6, "remarkably" means unremarkably or without any surprise.**

The survey found proportions that "remained remarkably consistent," contrary to an initial expectation of decline. Remarkably heightens how notable that consistency is; "unremarkably" cancels the adverb. The contrast with what researchers first expected is why the consistency earns remarkably. Defining it as without surprise reverses both the adverb and the survey's surprise framing.

The claim fails: remarkably marks surprise or note-worthiness, not the absence of surprise.

**C) In Paragraph 7, "documented" means recorded through careful observation.**

Researchers "have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns" in ostracods. Documented is the researcher's record of observed courtship flashes, not a casual rumour. The scientific setting—studying ostracods and their courtship displays—supports a careful observational sense. Recorded through careful observation is therefore the right gloss for that verb in context.

The ostracod line in paragraph 7 matches careful observational recording.

**D) In Paragraph 3, "fuses" means separates completely and permanently.**

The male permanently fuses to the female so tissues and circulatory systems merge. Fuse means join into one; "separates completely" is the antonym of that merger. Merging tissues and blood systems is joining, not splitting apart. The offered definition therefore reverses the reproductive attachment the paragraph describes.

The claim fails: fuses describes joining, not permanent separation.

**E) In Paragraph 9, "comprehensively" means only partially or incompletely.**

Paragraph 9 asks whether the full diversity of mechanisms will ever be comprehensively catalogued—i.e., covered thoroughly. Partially / incompletely would undercut "comprehensive," not define it. Full diversity paired with comprehensively points to a complete catalogue, not a partial one. The gloss "only partially" is therefore the opposite of the adverb's meaning in that closing question.

The claim fails: comprehensively means fully and thoroughly, not only in part.
highlights: deploying their light with a precision that suggests deliberate behavioural control
the proportion of glowing species remained remarkably consistent
have documented complex, species-specific flash patterns used during courtship displays
a much smaller male permanently fuses to the body of a female
Whether the full diversity of deep-sea bioluminescent mechanisms will ever be comprehensively catalogued

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage."
statements: Surprisingly, producing light can actually help an animal hide.
As expected, light always makes an animal easier to spot.
Unexpectedly, glowing can serve a concealment function instead.
Predictably, light exclusively reveals an animal's exact location.
Against expectation, emitting light can help conceal an animal.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Surprisingly, producing light can actually help an animal hide.**

The original says counterintuitively light can serve as camouflage. Surprisingly ≈ counterintuitively, and help an animal hide ≈ serve as camouflage, so both the surprise and the concealment keep pace. The paraphrase swaps wording but keeps the same unexpected function of light. Nothing in the line restores the everyday "light reveals" idea the original overturns.

The paraphrase preserves the unexpected hiding function of light.

**B) As expected, light always makes an animal easier to spot.**

As expected reverses counterintuitively, and easier to spot erases camouflage. The line restores the default "light reveals" intuition the original overturns. Always and easier to spot leave no room for the camouflage concession paragraph 5 introduces. Changing both the stance adverb and the function means this is an opposite claim, not a restatement.

**Trap:** Easier to spot feels like common sense about light, which is exactly what the original calls counterintuitive.

The paraphrase flips both the stance and the function, so it does not match.

**C) Unexpectedly, glowing can serve a concealment function instead.**

Unexpectedly tracks counterintuitively, and concealment function instead restates camouflage as an alternate use of glow. Wording changes, meaning holds. Instead signals the same surprise that light can hide rather than only reveal. The paraphrase therefore stays loyal to the original's unexpected concealment core.

The paraphrase keeps the surprise-plus-concealment core of the original.

**D) Predictably, light exclusively reveals an animal's exact location.**

Predictably and exclusively reveals invert the original on two axes: stance (surprise → predictability) and function (camouflage → pure revelation). Nothing of the camouflage concession survives. Exclusively blocks any hiding use, which is the opposite of light serving as camouflage. As a paraphrase check, both hinges fail, so the line cannot stand in for the original.

The paraphrase reverses the original, so it fails as a restatement.

**E) Against expectation, emitting light can help conceal an animal.**

Against expectation restates counterintuitively; emitting light … help conceal maps onto light as camouflage. Both hinge ideas remain. The stance adverb and the concealment function travel together, just as in the source sentence. That double match is what makes the line a true paraphrase rather than a near-miss.

The paraphrase matches the original's unexpected concealment claim.
highlights: Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage
Counterintuitively, light can also serve as camouflage

tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons total.
Most neurons are concentrated inside the central brain.
About two-thirds of neurons reside within the arms.
A severed arm can briefly continue grasping food.
Arm behaviour always requires central brain control.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons total.**

Paragraph (1) opens with the exact scale of octopus neural hardware: roughly 500 million neurons, a count compared to that of some small mammals. The statement simply restates that total figure; nothing in the sentence invents a different number or a different animal. The mammal comparison only supplies a scale cue — it does not change whose neurons are being counted. Match the claim to the opening quantity rather than to the vertebrate analogy that follows it.

**Tip:** When a claim recycles a named quantity from the first sentence of a paragraph, the matching span is almost always the proof.

The neuron total matches the passage figure, so the claim is true.

**B) Most neurons are concentrated inside the central brain.**

Paragraph (1) contrasts octopus organisation with vertebrates: rather than concentrating computational power in a single centralised brain, about two-thirds of the neurons sit in the arms. Saying "most" live in the central brain flips that architecture. "Most" would mean a majority in the brain, but the text places the majority in the arms and only implies a smaller share elsewhere. The rejection of a single centralised brain is the structural point of the sentence, so a brain-majority reading cannot stand.

**Trap:** "Comparable to mammals" can tempt you toward a mammal-style brain story; the text rejects that layout.

The claim reverses the passage's distributed layout, so it fails.

**C) About two-thirds of neurons reside within the arms.**

The same opening paragraph states that approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms, which is exactly what "about two-thirds… within the arms" paraphrases. The wording is faithful to both the proportion and the location. "Approximately" and "about" are interchangeable hedges here; neither upgrades nor downgrades the fraction. Location stays "within the arms," so no extra organs are smuggled into the claim.

That proportion is stated outright in paragraph (1), so the statement holds.

**D) A severed arm can briefly continue grasping food.**

Paragraph (2) describes an amputated arm that, still linked to its local neural cluster, can keep reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation. "Severed" and "amputated" name the same event; "briefly" mirrors "for a brief period." The local neural cluster explains how the behaviour can persist without the body, but the claim only needs the behaviour itself. Do not invent permanence — the text limits the episode to a short window after separation.

The severed-arm behaviour is described in those terms, so the claim matches the passage.

**E) Arm behaviour always requires central brain control.**

Paragraph (2) draws the opposite lesson: the amputated-arm episode suggests that at least some goal-directed behaviour does not strictly require centralised, brain-level control. The absolute "always" collapses that nuance into a universal rule the text denies. One counterexample of post-separation grasping is enough to break a rule that claims every arm action needs the central brain. Stay with "at least some" and "do not strictly require" rather than upgrading the lesson into a total ban on brain involvement.

**Trap:** Extreme words like always / never often fail when the text offers even one counterexample.

The passage says some arm behaviour need not depend on the central brain, so the absolute claim fails.
highlights: Octopuses possess roughly 500 million neurons, a number comparable to that of some small mammals
Rather than concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain, approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms
approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves
an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
at least some forms of goal-directed behaviour do not strictly require centralised, brain-level control at all

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Chromatophores are controlled via slow hormonal signalling.
Colour shifts can occur within roughly 200 milliseconds.
Iridophores help produce effects pigment alone cannot.
Octopus skin becomes physically rough during texture mimicry.
Octopuses possess multiple types of colour photoreceptors.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Chromatophores are controlled via slow hormonal signalling.**

Paragraph (3) says specialised skin cells called chromatophores are controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling. The statement swaps the actual control route for the slower pathway the text explicitly rejects. The words "rather than" mark hormonal signalling as the discarded alternative, not the mechanism in use. Fast colour change is explained by direct neural control; hormonal signalling is named only to be set aside.

**Trap:** The phrase "slower hormonal signalling" appears in the text as a contrast, not as the mechanism in use.

Nervous-system control, not hormonal signalling, is what the passage names, so the claim fails.

**B) Colour shifts can occur within roughly 200 milliseconds.**

The same camouflage paragraph states that an octopus can shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds — faster than a human blink. The statement lifts that timing figure without exaggeration. The blink comparison only dramatises speed; it does not replace the numeric window. Colour and pattern both shift in that interval, so a claim limited to colour still stays inside the given timing.

The 200-millisecond figure is stated directly, so the claim is true.

**C) Iridophores help produce effects pigment alone cannot.**

Paragraph (4) places iridophores and leucophores beneath the chromatophores and says they manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve. Credit to iridophores for those extra optical effects follows the text. Reflection and scattering are the tools; the point is that pigment layers are not enough on their own. Naming iridophores among those deeper layers is enough support even though leucophores share the job.

Iridophores are named for precisely that role, so the statement holds.

**D) Octopus skin becomes physically rough during texture mimicry.**

Paragraph (4) stresses that the animal can imitate coarse, rocky texture while its actual skin remains physically smooth throughout the transformation. Physical roughness of the skin is exactly what the passage rules out. Optical mimicry of rock texture is achieved by light effects, not by wrinkling or rasping the surface. Keep "looks rough" separate from "is rough" when the text insists the skin stays smooth.

**Trap:** Visual texture mimicry is not the same as a change in skin surface geometry.

The skin stays smooth, so the roughness claim fails.

**E) Octopuses possess multiple types of colour photoreceptors.**

Paragraph (5) opens by calling octopuses colour-blind and stating they possess only a single type of photoreceptor, unlike colour-sighted animals that rely on multiple types. "Multiple types" is the vertebrate contrast, not the octopus fact. Colour-blindness here is grounded in that single photoreceptor type, so inventing multiple types undoes the premise of the puzzle. Do not borrow the comparison animals' hardware and assign it to the octopus.

Only one photoreceptor type is attributed to octopuses, so the claim fails.
highlights: controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling
shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds, faster than the blink of a human eye
manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve
despite the animal's actual skin remaining physically smooth throughout the transformation
possessing only a single type of photoreceptor rather than the multiple types most colour-sighted animals rely on

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Octopuses have unscrewed jar lids for food.
Most octopus species live for several decades.
Females typically die shortly after eggs hatch.
Octopuses diverged from vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago.
Their nervous system shares direct inherited vertebrate ancestry.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Octopuses have unscrewed jar lids for food.**

Paragraph (6) lists laboratory feats that include several octopuses recorded unscrewing jar lids to reach food sealed inside. The statement is a clean paraphrase of that documented behaviour. The lab setting and the food motive stay intact; nothing upgrades the record into a wild-only claim or drops the goal. "Recorded" means observed cases exist, which is all the statement needs.

Jar-lid opening for food is explicitly recorded, so the claim matches the passage.

**B) Most octopus species live for several decades.**

Paragraph (7) says most octopus species live for only one to two years — an unusually short lifespan. "Several decades" stretches that window by orders of magnitude and contradicts the stated range. The text even flags the short life as unusual for such behavioural sophistication, so a decades-long reading fights both the number and the tone. Keep the one-to-two-year span and reject any paraphrase that multiplies it into decades.

**Trap:** Impressive cognition can make a long lifespan feel "natural"; the numbers say otherwise.

One-to-two-year lives overturn the decades claim, so it fails.

**C) Females typically die shortly after eggs hatch.**

The same lifespan paragraph states that females typically die shortly after their eggs hatch, after stopping eating during a prolonged brooding period. The statement tracks that typical pattern. "Typically" matches the passage's hedging, so you need not claim every female in every species. Brooding and fasting explain the sequence, but the claim itself only requires the post-hatching death pattern.

Female mortality after hatching is stated directly, so the claim holds.

**D) Octopuses diverged from vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago.**

Paragraph (8) places the evolutionary split: octopuses diverged from the lineage leading to vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago. The quantity and the comparator lineage are both intact in the paraphrase. "Lineage leading to vertebrates" is what "from vertebrates" compresses; the date stays the same. Do not confuse this deep split with the later claim about convergent, independent brain evolution.

The half-billion-year divergence figure is in the text, so the statement is true.

**E) Their nervous system shares direct inherited vertebrate ancestry.**

Paragraph (8) calls the octopus nervous system a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the vertebrate brain pathway, "rather than a shared inherited trait." Claiming direct inherited vertebrate ancestry is the model the text rejects. Independence is the key word: similar sophistication arose on a separate track, not by refining a common inherited brain plan. Treat "convergent" as the opposite of shared ancestry here, not as soft evidence for it.

Independence via convergent evolution overturns shared ancestry, so the claim fails.
highlights: Several octopuses have been recorded unscrewing jar lids to reach food sealed inside
most octopus species live for only one to two years, an unusually short lifespan
Females typically die shortly after their eggs hatch, having stopped eating entirely during a prolonged brooding period
octopuses diverged from the lineage leading to vertebrates roughly 500 million years ago
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Statements test whether an inference is actually supported, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Distributed neurons imply arms can act somewhat independently.
If arms hold two-thirds of neurons, one-third remains elsewhere.
Colour-blindness implies precise camouflage cannot possibly occur.
Short lifespan implies cognitive sophistication requires long-term learning.
Convergent evolution implies similar traits arose separately, not shared.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Distributed neurons imply arms can act somewhat independently.**

Paragraph (1) explains that putting roughly two-thirds of the neurons in the arms lets each arm process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain. Paragraph (2) then shows severed-arm grasping that does not require brain-level control. The inference follows those facts rather than leaping past them. "Somewhat independently" mirrors the text's "surprising degree of independence" without claiming the arms never consult the central brain. Local processing plus the amputated-arm example are enough warrant for that modest inference.

Arm-level independence is the direct implication of the distributed layout, so the claim holds.

**B) If arms hold two-thirds of neurons, one-third remains elsewhere.**

Paragraph (1) assigns approximately two-thirds of the neurons to the arms. Arithmetic closes the rest: the remaining one-third must sit outside the arms — chiefly in the central nervous system the paragraph contrasts with. The inference adds no new biological claim beyond that split. You are not inventing a new organ count; you are completing the fraction the text already gave. Nothing in the paragraph relocates that leftover third back into the arms.

**Tip:** When the text gives a clean fraction, the complementary fraction is usually fair game if nothing else relocates those neurons.

Two-thirds in the arms leaves one-third elsewhere, so the statement is sound.

**C) Colour-blindness implies precise camouflage cannot possibly occur.**

Paragraph (5) acknowledges colour-blindness and then discusses how octopuses still achieve camouflage precisely matched to surrounding colouration, including a skin-photoreceptor hypothesis. Colour-blindness raises a puzzle; it does not license the absolute "cannot possibly occur." The debate assumes the matching is real and asks how it works, so impossibility is the wrong inference. "Cannot possibly" is stronger than anything the researchers' open question supports.

**Trap:** A genuine research puzzle is not proof of impossibility.

Precise camouflage is described as real despite colour-blindness, so the impossibility claim fails.

**D) Short lifespan implies cognitive sophistication requires long-term learning.**

Paragraph (7) finds sophisticated behaviour especially puzzling given one-to-two-year lives — the short span is a tension with sophistication, not evidence that sophistication must rest on long-term learning. The "requires" leap is the reader's invention. The text never says complex behaviour depends on decades of practice; it only notes that short life makes such feats surprising. Puzzle language is not a causal rule about how intelligence must be acquired.

Short lifespan makes sophistication surprising rather than dependent on long learning, so the inference fails.

**E) Convergent evolution implies similar traits arose separately, not shared.**

Paragraph (8) defines the octopus case as convergent evolution entirely independent of the vertebrate pathway, not a shared inherited trait refined separately. That is exactly what "arose separately, not shared" means in this context. The "rather than a shared inherited trait" clause is the passage's own gloss of the term. Stay inside that contrast; do not redefine convergent as "coming together from one ancestor."

The passage's own contrast equates convergent evolution with separate origin, so the claim holds.
highlights: allowing each arm to process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain
approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves
researchers have long debated how they achieve camouflage so precisely matched to their surroundings' actual colouration
Such capabilities appear especially puzzling given that most octopus species live for only one to two years
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Statements require linking details across sections, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Distributed neurons help explain arm-level independent behaviour.
Colour-blindness and skin photoreceptors together suggest indirect colour sensing.
Short lifespan makes complex jar-opening behaviour easier to expect.
Convergent evolution helps explain why the nervous system differs from vertebrates.
Chromatophore speed and camouflage precision are entirely unrelated topics.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Distributed neurons help explain arm-level independent behaviour.**

Link paragraph (1)'s arm-resident neurons and local processing with paragraph (2)'s amputated-arm grasping: the distributed architecture is offered precisely as the reason arms can act with surprising independence. The synthesis stays inside what those sections supply. Paragraph (1) supplies the mechanism; paragraph (2) supplies a vivid consequence that does not need central control. You are joining those two stated pieces, not inventing a third theory of mind.

Distributed neurons are the mechanism the text uses for arm independence, so the claim holds.

**B) Colour-blindness and skin photoreceptors together suggest indirect colour sensing.**

Paragraph (5) pairs colour-blindness (one photoreceptor type) with the still-unconfirmed idea that specialised skin photoreceptors let the animal sense colour indirectly through the skin, independent of the eyes. Reading those two details together is how the hypothesis is framed. Eye-independent skin sensing is the proposed workaround for matching colour while colour-blind. Keep the claim at "suggest": the text never upgrades the hypothesis to proven fact.

**Tip:** "Suggest" is the right verb here — the text calls the idea influential but not conclusively confirmed.

Colour-blindness plus skin photoreceptors underwrite the indirect-sensing hypothesis, so the statement is true.

**C) Short lifespan makes complex jar-opening behaviour easier to expect.**

Paragraph (6) presents jar-opening and related feats as cognitive achievements hard to square with a simple nervous system; paragraph (7) then calls such capabilities especially puzzling given the one-to-two-year lifespan. Short life makes the behaviour harder to expect, not easier. Crossing the lab feats with the lifespan note should increase surprise, not reduce it. Any synthesis that says short life makes jar-opening "easier to expect" reverses the evaluative force of "puzzling."

**Trap:** Do not reverse the evaluative force of "puzzling."

The short lifespan deepens the puzzle rather than easing expectations, so the claim fails.

**D) Convergent evolution helps explain why the nervous system differs from vertebrates.**

Paragraph (1) establishes a layout "strikingly unlike" vertebrates; paragraph (8) explains that difference as convergent evolution on an independent pathway rather than shared inheritance. Convergent evolution is the evolutionary account of the structural difference. The early "unlike" description and the later independent-pathway story answer the same question from anatomy and from history. Shared inheritance is the rejected alternative, so convergence is what licenses the difference.

Independent convergent origins account for the unlike architecture, so the synthesis holds.

**E) Chromatophore speed and camouflage precision are entirely unrelated topics.**

Paragraphs (3)–(5) form one camouflage thread: rapid chromatophore shifts, deeper iridophore/leucophore effects, and the puzzle of precise colour matching despite colour-blindness. Speed and precision belong to the same capability story, not to disconnected chapters. Timing in (3) and matching accuracy in (5) are successive facets of how camouflage works. "Entirely unrelated" erases that continuous discussion and invents a split the passage never draws.

They sit inside one camouflage discussion, so "entirely unrelated" fails.
highlights: approximately two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside within its eight arms themselves, allowing each arm to process sensory information and initiate movement with a surprising degree of independence from the central brain
specialised photoreceptors distributed across the animal's own skin allow it to sense colour indirectly through the skin itself, entirely independent of its eyes

Such capabilities appear especially puzzling given that most octopus species live for only one to two years, an unusually short lifespan for an animal displaying this degree of behavioural sophistication
making their sophisticated nervous system a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains

Specialised skin cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling, allow an octopus to shift its skin colour and pattern within roughly 200 milliseconds

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "Had the arm not been severed, it would have remained attached."
"Researchers recommended that the lab documents each behaviour."
"The number of recorded cases continue to grow."
"Neither the pigment nor the reflection were fully understood."
"Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new theory."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "Had the arm not been severed, it would have remained attached."**

This is a third-conditional counterfactual with inversion: Had + past participle opens the if-clause, and would have + past participle carries the unreal past result. The negative not been severed pairs cleanly with the hypothetical remaining attached. The line is equivalent to If the arm had not been severed, it would have remained attached, only with Had-fronting. Both halves stay in the unreal-past frame, so tense and meaning align.

**Tip:** Inversion with Had is a formal stand-in for If the arm had not been severed…

The inverted third conditional is well formed, so the sentence stands.

**B) "Researchers recommended that the lab documents each behaviour."**

After recommend that, English expects the mandative subjunctive: a bare base verb. Documents is present indicative agreement with lab, so the line should read that the lab document each behaviour. Recommend, insist, and demand that all trigger this base-form pattern in formal English. The -s ending is the tell that the writer slipped back into ordinary present tense.

**Trap:** Ordinary third-person -s feels natural after a singular subject, but recommend that blocks that pattern.

The subjunctive needs document, not documents, so the wording fails — "Researchers recommended that the lab document each behaviour."

**C) "The number of recorded cases continue to grow."**

The grammatical subject is the number, which is singular; of recorded cases is only a prepositional phrase. A singular subject needs continues, not the plural continue. Cases is plural and sits next to the verb, which is why the ear wants continue — but cases is not the head. Strip the of-phrase and the agreement choice becomes obvious: the number continues.

**Tip:** Contrast the number of (singular verb) with a number of (usually plural verb).

Singular the number cannot take continue, so the line fails — "The number of recorded cases continues to grow."

**D) "Neither the pigment nor the reflection were fully understood."**

With neither…nor, the verb typically agrees with the nearer subject. Reflection is singular, so were should be was: Neither the pigment nor the reflection was fully understood. Pigment and reflection are both singular, so even a "both together" reading would not justify plural were. Proximity agreement is the reliable rule here and points only to was.

Proximity agreement picks singular was after reflection, so the wording does not hold — "Neither the pigment nor the reflection was fully understood."

**E) "Having observed the pattern, scientists proposed a new theory."**

The participle Having observed the pattern correctly attaches to scientists, the subject who did the observing and then proposed the theory. There is no dangling modifier or subject mismatch. The observers and the proposers are the same group, so the -ing opener is licensed. If the subject were something that cannot observe, the line would dangle; here it does not.

The participial opener belongs to scientists, so the sentence is sound.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide if each sentence is grammatically correct.
statements: "No sooner had the lid loosened than the octopus reached inside."
"The study, along with related trials, were published together."
"Each of the tested octopuses have solved the maze."
"By the time results arrive, theories will have already shifted."
"The samples, which were gathered carefully, reveal consistent behaviour."
tactical_explanations:
**A) "No sooner had the lid loosened than the octopus reached inside."**

No sooner…than requires inversion in the first clause: No sooner had + subject + past participle, then than + the following event. Here had the lid loosened pairs correctly with than the octopus reached inside. The pattern marks the second event as immediate after the first, which fits lid then reach. Swapping than for when would break the fixed correlative pair.

**Tip:** Prefer than (not when) after no sooner.

The No sooner…than inversion is correct, so the sentence stands.

**B) "The study, along with related trials, were published together."**

The head noun is the study; along with related trials is a parenthetical add-on and does not make the subject plural. The verb must be was published, not were published. Commas around the along with phrase advertise that trials are extra information, not a second head. Mentally delete that phrase and the singular verb snaps into place.

**Trap:** Material after along with / as well as / together with often tricks the ear into a plural verb.

Singular study needs was, so the wording fails — "The study, along with related trials, was published together."

**C) "Each of the tested octopuses have solved the maze."**

Each of takes a singular verb even when a plural noun follows of. Have solved should be has solved: Each of the tested octopuses has solved the maze. Octopuses looks plural and sits beside the verb, but each is the true subject and forces singular agreement. Replace each with all and plural have would fit — that contrast shows why have is wrong here.

Each demands singular has, so the line does not hold — "Each of the tested octopuses has solved the maze."

**D) "By the time results arrive, theories will have already shifted."**

By the time + present-time clause points to a future milestone; will have shifted is future perfect, placing the theories' change before that arrival. The tense pairing matches the deadline logic. Arrive stays present because by the time clauses often use present for future time; the perfect marks completion before that point. Already reinforces that the shift is finished relative to the results' arrival.

Future perfect correctly finishes the change before the later point, so the sentence is sound.

**E) "The samples, which were gathered carefully, reveal consistent behaviour."**

Samples is plural, so the non-restrictive which clause rightly uses were, and the main verb reveal stays plural. Agreement is consistent from relative clause through the main clause. Which refers to samples, not to a singular study or behaviour, so plural were is required inside the commas. The main clause then keeps the same plural head for reveal.

Plural samples are matched by were and reveal, so the wording holds.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 1, "centralised" means gathered into one main location.
In Paragraph 3, "specialised" means generic and unremarkable.
In Paragraph 5, "indirectly" means through a direct, immediate route.
In Paragraph 6, "reflexive" means automatic and unthinking.
In Paragraph 8, "convergent" means arising from a shared ancestor.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 1, "centralised" means gathered into one main location.**

Paragraph (1) contrasts concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain with the octopus's distributed arm neurons. In that contrast, centralised means gathered into one main location rather than spread across the arms. "Single…brain" and "concentrating…inside" are the local synonyms that lock the sense. Distributed arm neurons are the opposite pole, so centralised cannot mean scattered.

The surrounding "single…brain" contrast supports that sense, so the meaning claim is true.

**B) In Paragraph 3, "specialised" means generic and unremarkable.**

Paragraph (3) calls chromatophores specialised skin cells devoted to rapid colour and pattern change. Specialised here means adapted for a particular function; "generic and unremarkable" is the opposite of that context. The cells are introduced as the dedicated tools of camouflage, not as ordinary skin. A gloss that erases that dedicated role fights every cue in the sentence.

**Trap:** Do not invent a plain-English antonym when the cell name itself signals a dedicated role.

The word marks purpose-built cells, not bland ones, so the gloss fails.

**C) In Paragraph 5, "indirectly" means through a direct, immediate route.**

Paragraph (5) proposes that skin photoreceptors let the octopus sense colour indirectly through the skin, entirely independent of its eyes. Indirectly means through a non-eye, roundabout route — not a direct, immediate one. "Independent of its eyes" is the clarifying phrase: sensing bypasses the usual visual channel. A gloss that says "direct, immediate" simply flips the adverb.

The claimed gloss reverses the adverb, so the meaning claim fails.

**D) In Paragraph 6, "reflexive" means automatic and unthinking.**

Paragraph (6) says cognitive feats are difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system. Paired with simple, reflexive points to automatic, unthinking responses — the foil for jar-opening and maze skill. The feats are offered as too flexible and goal-directed for a purely reflexive account. That opposition fixes reflexive as automatic rather than as thoughtful or deliberative.

That contrast locks in the automatic sense, so the gloss holds.

**E) In Paragraph 8, "convergent" means arising from a shared ancestor.**

Paragraph (8) contrasts convergent evolution with "a shared inherited trait": the octopus pathway is independent of vertebrates. Convergent here means similar traits arising separately, not from a shared ancestor. The text's "rather than" clause is an on-page definition you can trust. Shared-ancestor wording belongs to the rejected model, not to convergent.

**Trap:** "Convergent" sounds like "coming together," but here it opposes shared ancestry.

The passage denies shared inheritance, so that gloss fails.
highlights: Rather than concentrating computational power inside a single centralised brain
Specialised skin cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by the nervous system rather than through slower hormonal signalling
allow it to sense colour indirectly through the skin itself, entirely independent of its eyes
difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system
a product of convergent evolution entirely independent from the evolutionary pathway that produced vertebrate brains, rather than a shared inherited trait

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide if the given meaning matches the word's actual use.
statements: In Paragraph 2, "amputated" means surgically or accidentally removed.
In Paragraph 4, "manipulate" means to skilfully influence or control.
In Paragraph 6, "reconcile" means to make consistent or compatible.
In Paragraph 7, "brooding" means actively hunting for new prey.
In Paragraph 9, "illuminate" means to make clearer or better understood.
tactical_explanations:
**A) In Paragraph 2, "amputated" means surgically or accidentally removed.**

Paragraph (2) discusses an amputated octopus arm continuing to reach and grasp after separation from the body. In that scene, amputated means the arm has been removed — whether by surgery or accident is secondary to the detachment itself. "Separation from the body" restates the same loss of attachment. The gloss stays at removal; it does not need a hospital setting to be correct.

Removal/separation is exactly what the context requires, so the gloss is true.

**B) In Paragraph 4, "manipulate" means to skilfully influence or control.**

Iridophores and leucophores "manipulate light reflection and scattering" to create effects pigment alone cannot achieve. That is skilful optical control of light, not social trickery. The objects of manipulate are physical light behaviours, so the lab sense of handling or steering fits. Do not import the everyday sense of deceitful influence into an optics sentence.

The light-control reading fits the optical layering, so the meaning holds.

**C) In Paragraph 6, "reconcile" means to make consistent or compatible.**

The cognitive feats are "difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system" — hard to make those behaviours fit, or sit consistently with, a purely reflexive model. That is the "make compatible" sense. The difficulty is intellectual: the feats and the simple model clash. Nothing in the line is about reconciling people after a quarrel.

Compatibility with a simple model is what the phrase questions, so the gloss is sound.

**D) In Paragraph 7, "brooding" means actively hunting for new prey.**

Paragraph (7) describes a prolonged brooding period during which females stop eating entirely until eggs hatch. Brooding here is egg-guarding, not hunting; the fasting undercuts any "actively hunting" reading. Months of not eating while eggs develop is care behaviour, the opposite of foraging. Hunting would require feeding, which the sentence explicitly suspends.

**Trap:** Everyday "brooding" (moodiness) and biological brooding (egg care) are both unlike hunting.

Egg-tending, not prey-hunting, is the sense in use, so the gloss fails.

**E) In Paragraph 9, "illuminate" means to make clearer or better understood.**

Paragraph (9) asks whether studying octopus cognition will "meaningfully illuminate general principles" of how intelligence can arise. Illuminate here is figurative clarification — making principles clearer — not physical lighting. The object is principles of intelligence, an abstract target that only the "make clearer" sense can take. Physical light fixtures belong to paragraph (6), not to this debate question.

Making general principles better understood matches the debate frame, so the claim holds.
highlights: an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
which manipulate light reflection and scattering to produce effects chromatophore pigment alone cannot achieve
cognitive feats difficult to reconcile with a simple, reflexive nervous system
having stopped eating entirely during a prolonged brooding period that can last several months
Whether studying octopus cognition will meaningfully illuminate general principles of how intelligence can arise

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: One sentence from the passage, followed by five short paraphrases. Decide if each preserves its meaning. Original: "An amputated octopus arm can continue reaching toward and grasping food."
statements: A severed arm can still reach for and grab food.
A severed arm immediately stops moving entirely.
A detached arm remains capable of grasping food briefly.
An intact, attached arm can reach toward food normally.
A removed arm continues performing food-directed movements.
tactical_explanations:
**A) A severed arm can still reach for and grab food.**

The original says an amputated octopus arm can continue reaching toward and grasping food. Severed ≈ amputated, reach for ≈ reaching toward, and grab ≈ grasping; the paraphrase keeps the same actor and action. "Still" covers the continuation after separation without adding new timing claims. No intact-arm subject and no total stop are smuggled in.

Same arm, same food-directed reaching, so the paraphrase preserves the meaning.

**B) A severed arm immediately stops moving entirely.**

The source claim is continued reaching and grasping after amputation, not total stillness. "Immediately stops moving entirely" reverses both the motion and the brief persistence of the behaviour. Every key verb in the original (continue, reaching, grasping) is negated by stop and entirely. That is a meaning flip, not a near miss.

**Trap:** Absolute stop language is the near-miss false when the text stresses continuation.

Continued grasping overturns total cessation, so this paraphrase fails.

**C) A detached arm remains capable of grasping food briefly.**

Detached matches amputated/separated, grasping food matches the original action, and briefly reflects paragraph (2)'s "for a brief period." The paraphrase stays faithful while importing that short-duration cue from the same sentence. Capability language ("remains capable") is a fair restatement of can continue, not an upgrade to permanent skill. Subject, action, and duration all track the source.

Capability plus brief duration both track the passage, so the meaning holds.

**D) An intact, attached arm can reach toward food normally.**

The original is about an amputated arm after separation. Shifting to an intact, attached arm quietly changes the subject and drops the surprising post-separation behaviour the sentence exists to report. Normal reaching by an attached arm may be true in life, but it is not what this line says. Paraphrase checks subject identity first; here the subject has been swapped.

**Trap:** A bland true-sounding fact about normal arms is still a wrong paraphrase of this line.

The intact-arm rewrite abandons the amputated subject, so it does not preserve the meaning.

**E) A removed arm continues performing food-directed movements.**

Removed restates amputated, and "continues performing food-directed movements" compresses "continue reaching toward and grasping food" without adding or contradicting content. Food-directed covers both reaching toward and grasping without inventing a new goal. The continuation after removal is preserved, so the paraphrase stays loyal to the original event.

Removal plus continued food-directed motion match the original, so the paraphrase stands.
highlights: an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
an amputated octopus arm, still connected to its own local neural cluster, can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body
can continue reaching toward and grasping food for a brief period after separation from the body

tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included and increased vocabulary precision.
statements: The three-sector model's originators framed structural transformation as a near-universal consequence of rising income, not mere coincidence.
South Korea's structural transformation is described as having taken considerably longer than comparable European transitions.
Deindustrialization is described as occurring exclusively where manufacturing output genuinely contracts.
US manufacturing's employment share fell below 9% even as real output roughly tripled.
The quaternary sector proposal treats codified, specialised knowledge as analytically indispensable to its distinction from tertiary services.
tactical_explanations:
**A) The three-sector model's originators framed structural transformation as a near-universal consequence of rising income, not mere coincidence.**

Paragraph 1 says the originators framed the trajectory as "a near-universal consequence of rising income and shifting consumer demand rather than a mere historical coincidence." The statement restates that causal framing faithfully — rising income drives the shift; coincidence is rejected. Notice the passage pairs rising income with shifting consumer demand; the statement's focus on rising income still tracks the same anti-coincidence framing without inventing a new cause. If you paraphrase, keep the "rather than…coincidence" contrast intact so the verdict stays locked to the originators' wording.

**Tip:** Match the exact framing words (near-universal, rising income, coincidence) before you decide.

The claim tracks Paragraph 1's wording, so it is true.

**B) South Korea's structural transformation is described as having taken considerably longer than comparable European transitions.**

Paragraph 1 calls Korea's change "a compression of structural transformation that took many earlier-industrialising European economies well over a century to accomplish." Compressed means shorter, not longer — the trap flips the comparison. The European century-plus span is the slow baseline; Korea is the compressed case that finished the same kind of shift faster. Reading "took…well over a century" as if it described Korea, rather than Europe, is how the chronology gets reversed.

**Trap:** Chronology flip — "longer" reverses what "compression" means.

The statement reverses the passage's time comparison, so it fails.

**C) Deindustrialization is described as occurring exclusively where manufacturing output genuinely contracts.**

Paragraph 2 says deindustrialization draws scrutiny "precisely because it appears to unfold even where manufacturing itself remains robust rather than genuinely contracting." "Exclusively where…contracts" is the opposite of that point. The text's interest is the robust-output case, not a contraction-only rule; "exclusively" erases the very scenario the paragraph highlights. Match "remains robust rather than genuinely contracting" before accepting any absolute about where deindustrialization occurs.

**Trap:** Absolute "exclusively" ignores the robust-output case the text stresses.

The claim invents a contraction-only rule the passage rejects, so it is false.

**D) US manufacturing's employment share fell below 9% even as real output roughly tripled.**

Paragraph 2 gives both figures together: employment share fell "to under 9% by 2020, even as manufacturing output, adjusted for inflation, roughly tripled." The statement pairs those facts without twisting either one. "Under 9%" and "roughly tripled" are the same thresholds; "adjusted for inflation" is what "real" output signals in the paraphrase. Keep both halves of the "even as" pairing — employment down, output up — or the divergence claim collapses.

The numeric pairing matches Paragraph 2 exactly, so the claim holds.

**E) The quaternary sector proposal treats codified, specialised knowledge as analytically indispensable to its distinction from tertiary services.**

Paragraph 3 contrasts information-intensive work with routine tertiary services by "heavy reliance on specialised, codified knowledge," and calls that distinction "analytically indispensable." The statement captures both the knowledge criterion and its analytical weight. Retail and hospitality are the routine foil; software, finance, and research sit on the knowledge-intensive side of the same contrast. If a choice drops "analytically indispensable" or swaps in a weaker motive, it no longer matches the proponents' rationale in Paragraph 3.

The proposal's own rationale supports the claim, so it is true.
highlights: framed as a near-universal consequence of rising income and shifting consumer demand rather than a mere historical coincidence
a compression of structural transformation that took many earlier-industrialising European economies well over a century to accomplish
even where manufacturing itself remains robust rather than genuinely contracting
fell from around 24% in 1970 to under 9% by 2020, even as manufacturing output, adjusted for inflation, roughly tripled
a distinction proponents consider analytically indispensable

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Statements test close reading comprehension in order, with one numeric statement included.
statements: Quinary sector boundaries are described as consistently tracked as a separate category by all national statistical agencies.
The 2018 study's divergence pattern is described as a mere artefact of US-specific statistical conventions.
Manufacturing value added grew in 33 of the 38 economies where employment share had declined.
The Sub-Saharan African employment-GDP gap is attributed mainly to inherent, unchangeable limitations of agriculture itself.
Underinvestment in technology and infrastructure is cited as a contributing factor to low agricultural output per worker.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Quinary sector boundaries are described as consistently tracked as a separate category by all national statistical agencies.**

Paragraph 4 says boundaries "remain genuinely contested and are applied inconsistently," with some agencies folding quinary activities "directly back into broader tertiary or quaternary categories." "Consistently…by all" invents uniformity the text denies. Folding activities back into tertiary or quaternary is the opposite of tracking them as a clean separate series. Treat any "all agencies / consistently separate" wording as a red flag against Paragraph 4's caution about cross-country comparisons.

**Trap:** "All…consistently" overstates what contested, inconsistent practice allows.

The claim fails because agencies do not track quinary as one neat separate category.

**B) The 2018 study's divergence pattern is described as a mere artefact of US-specific statistical conventions.**

Paragraph 5 opens by saying the US employment–output divergence "is by no means unique to it, nor is it merely an artefact of one country's particular statistical conventions," then cites the 42-economy study. Calling the pattern a US-only artefact reverses that framing. The multi-country evidence is introduced precisely to show the pattern travels beyond one nation's bookkeeping.
